text:
alex: FYI saw a tiny regression in tail p99 on the kv cache experiments after the new eviction fast-path landed. digging in now, but posting here in case it's obvious to others.
maria: ack. which workload / trace?
alex: two traces: long-conversation chat sim and a synthetic replay hitting many prefixes. p99 jumped ~18% on the chat trace after about 300s of sustained longctx.
cheng: can you paste the profiler snippet?
alex: pasted below — this is ~10s around the spike, sampled perf + allocator logs:
```
[perf] top: kv_cache::page_walk 42% | kv_cache::compact 8% | runtime::forward 15%
[alloc] kv_pages_reserved=12432, kv_pages_inuse=11988, page_frags=0.26
[evict] aggressive_eviction=true, candidates=312 -> selected=1
```
maria: interesting that page_walk dominates. suggests more scanning when many prefixes partially overlap. might be fragmentation + linear probe cost.
cheng: could be our cache key canonicalization producing slightly different keys for the same logical prefix across requests (salt/order noise). that would reduce reuse and cause more page_walks.
sophie: infra-bot: note: rolled back eviction-fastpath on prod canary 3 to stabilize p99 at 16:12 UTC.
alex: yeah rollback helped but still seeing some longctx mem growth in canary. hypothesis: some prefix sequences create chain collisions in the page map -> rare linear scans escalate.
maria: two quick experiments to run: 1) add a short canonicalization pass that normalizes whitespace and lowercases non-sensitive prefix tokens before hashing; 2) sample frequent prefix families and track reuse rate pre/post.
cheng: +1. also propose we add a tiny per-request sticky-hint: if request matches previous session prefix fingerprint, mark those pages as hot for N=5s to avoid immediate eviction churn. cheap to implement and might reduce p99.
alex: i'll run experiment 1 (canonicalization) on the replay and collect `kv_hit_rate_by_prefix` and `page_walk_ops_per_prefix`. will post results.
sophie: infra-bot: created job job/kv-prefix-sample-4390001234 (runs on canary infra)
maria: if canonicalization reduces distinct key cardinality by >3% we should consider permanent accept. if not, we try sticky-hint. also let's avoid adding global locks — prefer per-shard hints.
cheng: note: kernel selection/batching unrelated here but keep in mind batching increases contiguity of prefixes which could change fragmentation profile. so rerun with both single-request and batched replays.
alex: noted. timeline: run canonicalization + single and batched replays in the next 2 hrs, post metrics.
maria: thanks — add the metrics: p50/p95/p99, kv_hit_rate, page_walk_rate, page_frags, eviction_rate. that should tell a story.
alex: will do. if anyone wants access to the replay or profiler results ping me and i'll share GCS link.
sophie: :thumbsup:
